ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the attached figure there is a triangle RQS, R is located at the lower left, Q is located at the middle-left position, and S is located at the upper right. The diagram marks RQ = 21, QS = 33.2, RS = 53; the requested x° is the angle at point R formed by sides RQ and RS. Then reason: The side opposite angle x is QS, so use the Law of Cosines: cos(x) = (RQ^2 + RS^2 - QS^2) / (2·RQ·RS) = (21^2 + 53^2 - 33.2^2) / (2·21·53). Calculating gives cos(x) = (441 + 2809 - 1102.24) / 2226 = 2147.76 / 2226 ≈ 0.9649, so x ≈ arccos(0.9649) ≈ 15.3°. Rounded to the nearest integer as required, x = 15°.
